title: Splitting and Cleaning Strings
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of splitting and cleaning strings in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply splitting and cleaning strings in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to processing user input and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Splitting and Cleaning Strings through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding splitting and cleaning strings helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Splitting and Cleaning Strings helps you reason about split. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: split. Then connect it to strip , chomp , and chop. The remaining syllabus points—Whitespace normalization, Processing user input—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Run the example as written, compare it with the expected result, and explain why each line supports splitting and cleaning strings. Next change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.

content_blocks.title: Recap
